dimension_justifications.soundness: The finite-pool realized-schedule estimand is coherent, descriptive and inferential language is disciplined, contrast directions are consistent, and the printed arithmetic checks out. However, every central result is source-reported and cannot be verified because the paired records, stochastic traces, implementations, construction artifacts, and evidence-ID crosswalk are absent.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The title gives a bounded identity, the paper is logically organized, tables are legible, caveats are placed early and beside relevant claims, and the defined-versus-disclosed protocol boundary is unusually explicit. Presentation remains below excellent because the unexplained phrase “source manuscript” obscures result provenance, “ground-truth injection” can be misread as answer-label leakage, status terminology is dense and repetitive, and Table 1 is called canonical despite omitting disclosed rows.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The paper contributes a careful organization of previously reported protocol contrasts and an explicit finite-pool, realized-trace interpretation. It explicitly does not introduce a scorer or isolate a mechanism; combined with one model-task setting, missing anti_inject outcomes, one stochastic realization, and unreplayable evidence, the decision-relevant contribution is narrow.

paper_summary: This paper presents an exploratory descriptive audit of multiple-choice scoring protocols for LLaDA-8B-Instruct on constructed GSM8K-MC pools. It organizes source-reported comparisons among s_conf, mc_uniform, rand_inject, and fixed_inject, distinguishes nominal scoring-draw matching from forward-call-count matching, and highlights an aggregate fixed-order advantage that reverses for answer position 0. All empirical results are explicitly conditioned on named finite pools and recorded scorer realizations, with no inferential, causal, actual-cost, or cross-setting interpretation.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest verifiable contribution is the disciplined presentation boundary: Equation 1 defines a finite-pool realized-schedule contrast, Tables 3–6 use consistent contrast directions, and the displayed arithmetic is internally correct—for example, (106−54)/400=13.0%, (145−99)/819=5.62%, and (21−46)/199=−12.56%. The paper also clearly distinguishes five source-defined arms from the four arms with disclosed outcomes.
strengths: The title, Introduction, and Section 2 consistently identify the work as an exploratory protocol audit rather than a new scoring method or component-level causal study.
The global SR/CV notation on PDF page 1 and local qualifications in table captions prevent the reader from mistaking source-reported values for independently reproduced measurements.

Section 3 and Tables 2 and 7 clearly distinguish protocol definitions, scoring draws, selection calls, total model-invocation counts, and actual resource costs; the paper explicitly avoids equating call counts with FLOPs, latency, memory, or energy.

The finite-pool realized-schedule estimand on PDF page 3 is well aligned with the descriptive language. The paper appropriately omits confidence intervals, p-values, and cross-pool inference after declining to posit a probability model.
The b/c/m definitions and contrast orientations are consistent. Table 5 places the answer-position-0 reversal next to the aggregate, making the caveat difficult to miss.

The defined-versus-disclosed boundary is exceptionally explicit: anti_inject is defined but repeatedly identified as lacking disclosed outcomes, and the paper does not claim a complete five-arm comparison.
The novelty boundary in Section 2 is restrained and clear: confidence-guided scoring is attributed to iLLaDA, while the claimed contribution is limited to the present protocol and budget audit.

All eight PDF pages are readable. The manuscript has five main-text pages before references, remains within the nine-page main-text limit, uses an ICLR review header, and contains no apparent author or institutional identifiers.
The AI-assistance disclosure on PDF page 5 clearly separates language/LaTeX/review assistance from experimental evidence generation or verification.
questions: What exactly is the repeatedly referenced “source manuscript”: an earlier internal draft by the same anonymous authors, an external unpublished source, or another artifact? Who executed the original experiments whose values are transcribed here?
Does “ground-truth-token injection” mean teacher-forcing each candidate option string independently, including tokens of incorrect options, rather than injecting the correct answer label?
What tie-breaking rule determines the next revealed token when multiple remaining positions have equal minimum loss for s_conf or equal maximum loss for anti_inject?
Why is Table 1 titled the “Canonical map of disclosed results” when it omits the single-draw row from Table 3 and the pilot and pooled-disclosure rows from Table 4?
Can an anonymous replayable bundle for E10–E14 be supplied so that pool construction, predictions, b/c counts, recorded stochastic traces, and call accounting can be recomputed?
How sensitive are the s_conf–rand_inject and s_conf–mc_uniform contrasts to additional reveal-order and mask-draw realizations?

issues.location: PDF page 1, Abstract and Evidence notation, lines 16–34; page 5, Section 6, lines 242–254; page 8, Appendix D, Tables 9–10
issues.observed_evidence: The paper and reviewer-safe inventory explicitly state that every empirical value is source-reported/cannot-verify. The paired item records, prompts, choice-construction code, model/tokenizer revisions, protocol implementations, stochastic traces, analysis code, call traces, and E10–E15 crosswalk are absent. This demonstrates an artifact absence, not that the printed results are false.
issues.why_it_matters: The central contribution is empirical, so internal arithmetic consistency cannot establish that the pools, predictions, discordance counts, or protocol executions are genuine and correctly labeled. The paper is therefore not decision-ready as an empirical conference submission.
issues.required_fix: Provide a hashed anonymous experimental bundle resolving E10–E14, including item and pool identifiers, construction metadata, prompt/model/tokenizer revisions, arm configurations and implementations, recorded mask draws and reveal orders, per-option scores and predictions, paired aggregation code, call traces, and a complete evaluated-arm ledger. If recovery is impossible, reposition the work explicitly as a non-empirical methodological note and remove claims that depend on unavailable measurements.
issues.verification_test: Starting only from the anonymous bundle and documented command, reconstruct every choice set, verify n=400/fresh-pool balance and disjointness, replay every disclosed arm, and reproduce Tables 3–6 exactly, including accuracies, b/c or m counts, effect directions, and rounded percentage-point values. Confirm hashes before recomputation.
issues.evidence_needed: Resolvable E10–E14 artifacts plus a manifest, environment lock, and canonical replay command.

issues.location: PDF page 1, Abstract lines 16 and 23 and Introduction lines 43–49; page 2, Section 3 lines 98–109; page 5, Section 6 lines 242–259
issues.observed_evidence: The manuscript repeatedly attributes definitions and measurements to “the source manuscript” but never identifies what that phrase denotes or whether the present authors ran the underlying experiments. It simultaneously presents the audit as this paper's contribution and says no experiment or analysis was rerun “for this revision.”
issues.why_it_matters: A fresh reader cannot determine the paper's basic identity: original empirical study, reanalysis of the authors' earlier records, or secondary audit of external unpublished work. This ambiguity obstructs assessment of contribution ownership, evidence provenance, and reproducibility.
issues.required_fix: Define the source unambiguously at first use. State, without breaking anonymity, who generated the original records, whether the source is an earlier internal version of this work or an external document, what material was available to the authors, and what transformations produced the present tables. Replace vague “source manuscript” wording with a consistent provenance term.
issues.verification_test: Give the revised paper to a reader who has no revision history and ask them to identify who ran the experiments, what artifact supplied the numbers, what the present paper newly contributes, and which steps were rerun. All four answers should be explicit from the Abstract/Introduction and evidence section alone.
issues.evidence_needed: A clear provenance statement and, if the source is external, a citable or anonymously accessible source artifact; if internal, a description of the original experimental record and the present authors' relationship to it.

issues.location: PDF page 3, Section 3, Equation 1 and lines 138–153; page 4, Section 5.1 and Table 4; page 5, Section 6 lines 235–245; page 6, Appendix A lines 303–308
issues.observed_evidence: The random-order result uses one unavailable schedule, and each mc_uniform budget uses one unavailable stored collection of mask draws. The paper correctly defines a realized-schedule estimand and explicitly disclaims an expectation over stochastic policies.
issues.why_it_matters: The estimand is coherent, but it establishes only that particular unavailable traces produced different outputs. Without replication across scorer randomness, the result provides little evidence about the scoring protocols readers would deploy and cannot distinguish a stable protocol difference from realization sensitivity.
issues.required_fix: Retain the realized-trace results but add a frozen multi-realization evaluation for rand_inject and mc_uniform, reporting the distribution across independently generated, replayable schedules or mask streams. Clearly separate finite-pool variation from scorer-randomness variation.
issues.verification_test: Using published seeds and stored traces, independently replay every realization; confirm identical predictions; report per-realization contrasts and show whether the headline directions and practically relevant magnitudes persist across realizations.
issues.evidence_needed: Multiple replayable reveal-order schedules and mask-draw streams, per-realization item-level predictions, and a prespecified aggregation protocol.

issues.location: PDF page 1, Abstract lines 16–18 and Introduction lines 50–53; pages 2–3, Section 3 lines 106–120 and Table 2
issues.observed_evidence: The central arm is called “ground-truth-token injection,” while the method describes revealing a known candidate token during scoring. The paper does not explicitly say that this occurs separately for every candidate, including incorrect options. It calls the confidence schedule deterministic but gives only final option-score tie breaking, not the within-schedule rule for equal token losses.
issues.why_it_matters: “Ground truth” can be misread as leakage of the correct answer label, obscuring the protocol's identity. Missing schedule tie handling also leaves the supposedly deterministic protocol incompletely specified.
issues.required_fix: At first use, state that each candidate continuation is teacher-forced independently and that “ground truth” is relative to the candidate sequence, not the task's correct-answer label; preferably use “candidate-token feedback.” Define the exact within-schedule tie rule for s_conf and anti_inject.
issues.verification_test: Construct a two-option toy example with an incorrect candidate and tied token losses. The revised definition and reference implementation should uniquely determine the injected tokens, reveal order, and selected option without consulting undocumented conventions.
issues.evidence_needed: Precise protocol prose plus a tie-case unit test or pseudocode.

issues.location: PDF page 2, Table 1 and lines 54–76; page 4, Tables 3–4
issues.observed_evidence: Table 1 is titled the “Canonical map of disclosed results,” yet it excludes the single-draw +14.0 pp row shown in Table 3 and the pilot and pooled-disclosure rows shown in Table 4. The table is therefore a selected headline map rather than a complete map of disclosed results.
issues.why_it_matters: Because the paper emphasizes incomplete reporting and post-selection boundaries, “canonical” can incorrectly imply a complete endpoint ledger and weakens the otherwise careful distinction between defined, evaluated, disclosed, and foregrounded arms.
issues.required_fix: Either include every disclosed quantitative row in Table 1 or rename it “Map of foregrounded and selected contrasts,” explicitly list the omitted disclosures, and reserve “complete” or “canonical” for a verified exhaustive ledger.
issues.verification_test: Cross-check every quantitative result row in Tables 3–6 against Table 1. Either all appear, or the caption and a footnote identify exactly which classes are intentionally excluded and why.
issues.evidence_needed: A complete row crosswalk or narrower table title and caption.

issues.location: PDF page 5, Section 6, “What the current package contains,” lines 247–254; page 8, Appendix D lines 409–411; frozen MANIFEST.json
issues.observed_evidence: The heading says “What the current package contains,” but the paragraph describes a separate authoring directory containing TeX, bibliography, build products, and legacy figures. The actual frozen reviewer bundle contains the PDF, source hashes, and reviewer-safe summaries, not those source files or legacy assets.
issues.why_it_matters: Readers may incorrectly infer that manuscript source or reusable artifacts accompany the submission. The distinction among authoring directory, frozen review bundle, and any eventual public artifact is not explicit.
issues.required_fix: Name each package separately and provide an exact included-file statement matching the frozen or public manifest. Move details about unused legacy authoring assets to an appendix unless they are relevant to reproducibility.
issues.verification_test: Compare the revised availability paragraph line-by-line with MANIFEST.json; every claimed included file must resolve within the stated bundle, and every inaccessible authoring-only item must be labeled as such.
issues.evidence_needed: A package-specific manifest and revised availability wording.

issues.location: PDF page 1, Abstract and Evidence notation; page 2, Table 1; pages 3–5, result-table captions and Conclusion
issues.observed_evidence: Before stating the simple study identity, the Abstract layers “foregrounded matched-draw,” “separately identified,” “post-selected matched-forward-call-count sensitivity,” “displayed point,” “finite pools,” and SR/CV caveats. Nearly identical status boundaries are then repeated in the global notation, Table 1, each result caption, nearby prose, Limitations, and Conclusion.
issues.why_it_matters: The caution is scientifically appropriate, but the density and repetition make the abstract harder to parse and obscure the main research question. Status vocabulary risks becoming a second conceptual system readers must decode alongside the protocols and budgets.
issues.required_fix: Preserve all material caveats while simplifying the Abstract to the question, setting, principal descriptive observations, and one compact evidence-boundary sentence. Use a small, consistent status vocabulary defined once, with only claim-specific caveats repeated locally.
issues.verification_test: Audit the revision against a caveat checklist to ensure no limitation is lost, then ask an unfamiliar reader to summarize the question, protocols, principal observations, and evidence boundary after reading only the Abstract and Table 1.
issues.evidence_needed: A terminology crosswalk and a compressed Abstract/summary table.

ethics_concerns: No human-subject, privacy, safety-deployment, or sensitive-data issue is apparent from the frozen snapshot. The paper makes no measured resource-efficiency claim and includes an explicit AI-assistance disclosure. The phrase “ground-truth injection” should nevertheless be clarified to avoid implying answer-label leakage.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by A14-R02-C as a fresh, isolated AI reviewer for internal pre-submission quality control. It used only the frozen round-2 submission snapshot and did not communicate with authors or other reviewers.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A hashed anonymous bundle that independently reproduces all accuracies, b/c or m counts, pool properties, contrast directions, and call-accounting rows in Tables 3–7.
Replayable multi-realization results showing that the random-order and random-mask conclusions are stable across schedules and mask streams.
A complete evaluated-arm outcome matrix, including anti_inject or a documented reason it was never evaluated, together with decision chronology that resolves selective-reporting concerns.
An explicit, reader-facing explanation of what the “source manuscript” is, who generated the measurements, and what analysis this paper newly contributes.
A precise candidate-token-feedback definition and deterministic tie rule, plus concise protocol pseudocode.
Replication of the matched-L observation on an independently constructed pool or additional model/task settings, which would materially increase significance beyond the present setting-local audit.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Recomputation that changes the sign or materially changes the magnitude of the +13.0 pp matched-L result, the +5.62 pp aggregate fixed-order result, or the position-0 reversal.
Evidence that the n=400 and n=819 pools overlap, are not balanced as described, or use materially different prompts or choice sets across arms.
A complete arm ledger showing that omitted evaluated arms or budgets contradict the foregrounded narrative.
Multi-realization evaluation showing that reported random-order or random-mask effects are atypical or directionally unstable.
Instrumented traces contradicting the reported L/2L call accounting or showing that purportedly paired arms were not evaluated on identical recorded choice sets.
Evidence that “source manuscript” denotes external work without appropriate attribution or that the present authors cannot establish provenance for the transcribed measurements.
review_limitations: The review was restricted to the eight-page PDF and reviewer-safe evidence, provenance, manifest, schema, and citation-lock materials in the frozen snapshot.
No item-level record, implementation, stochastic trace, or resolvable E10–E15 artifact was available, so empirical claims were assessed as cannot_verify rather than demonstrated false.
Internet and external-source inspection were prohibited; citation assessment therefore relied only on the included partial citation lock.
Printed arithmetic, terminology, organization, tables, anonymity, and ICLR page-format compliance were checked directly across the entire PDF.
